evals.name: htmleez-shelf-members
evals.prompt: my shelf app renders html with htmleez (lib/server.dart, lib/views/). tailwind v4 + basecoat-css 1.0.2 are already installed through npm and the css/js are served from /assets. the basecoat jinja templates are already in templates/basecoat and lib/basecoat/basecoat.dart is set up. write lib/views/members.dart with a `HTML membersPage(List<Member> members)` where Member has int id, String name, String email, String role. i want a table of members with a per-row actions dropdown (Edit -> /members/<id>/edit, Remove -> hx-delete on /members/<id>, should look dangerous), and an 'Invite member' button that opens a dialog with an email input and a role select (admin/member/viewer, member preselected). names come from user signups so be careful.
evals.expected_output: A Dart file using htmleez for page markup and the bundled Basecoat interface (bc.dropdownMenu, bc.dialog, bc.select) bridged with Raw(...), with per-row ids, user data escaped in content positions, and plain Basecoat 1.0 markup for table/field/buttons.
assertions: Calls bc.dropdownMenu, bc.dialog and bc.select from the bundled interface instead of hand-writing those three structures
Macro output enters the htmleez tree through Raw(...) (directly or via a helper)
Dialog body is produced as an HTML string (toHtml() or a string), not passed as an HTML node
Each row's dropdown gets a unique id derived from member.id
The dialog and the select are given explicit ids
Member names in content positions are escaped (.t or esc(...)), never interpolated raw into a label, title or body
Remove item carries hx-delete in attrs and is marked destructive (data-variant="destructive")
Dropdown and dialog triggers are styled through triggerAttrs with class btn
Role select uses BcItem values admin/member/viewer with selected: 'member'
Form controls sit in div[role=group].field and the select's label targets <id>-trigger
Uses no pre-1.0 compound classes (btn-outline, btn-destructive, ...)
Table with row menus is not wrapped in .table-container

evals.name: jaspr-settings-page
evals.prompt: I'm building an admin site with Jaspr 0.23 in server mode (lib/main.server.dart, pages in lib/pages/). Basecoat's CSS is loaded and I vendored the jinja templates into templates/basecoat with lib/basecoat/basecoat.dart next to them. Add lib/pages/settings.dart with a SettingsPage component: tabs for 'Profile' and 'Notifications'. Profile has a name input and a timezone picker using the fancy Basecoat select grouped by continent (a handful of zones is fine), with the user's current zone preselected from a `String timezone` constructor param. Notifications has two switches. Also tell me anything I need to change outside that file.
evals.expected_output: A Jaspr component file that renders Basecoat macros through RawText in server-rendered components, builds slot content as HTML strings, uses plain Jaspr markup for non-macro components, and notes the JS script and server-only import requirements.
assertions: Macro output is rendered with RawText(...) (not the deprecated raw(), not text())
Uses bc.select with BcGroup/BcItem and selected taken from the timezone param
Uses bc.tabs with BcTab entries, or hand-writes .tabs markup as Jaspr elements with correct roles and ids
Content passed into macro slots (tab panels) is an HTML string, not a Jaspr Component
select and tabs calls have explicit stable ids
No macro call sits inside a @client component
Switches are native checkboxes with role="switch" and inputs are wrapped in .field
Uses Jaspr 0.23 API: Component build(BuildContext) and package:jaspr/dom.dart elements
Mentions that Basecoat JavaScript must be loaded (Document head or script tag)
Mentions keeping the Basecoat instance or FileSystemLoader out of client-compiled code
Uses no pre-1.0 compound classes

evals.name: setup-and-jinja-layout
evals.prompt: we have a small dart shelf backend (bin/server.dart) and want to start rendering html pages from it with jinja templates + basecoat, like our old flask app did. package.json already has tailwindcss 4 and basecoat-css 1.0.2 and builds web/app.css. set everything up: the templates, a base layout with a sidebar (Dashboard, Projects, Settings groups whatever makes sense, current page highlighted) and a toaster, and a /projects page that lists `projects` (id, name, status) with a status select per row. we ship this as a `dart compile exe` binary in a scratch docker image so it can't depend on files lying around at runtime. show me the commands i need to run too.
evals.expected_output: Setup steps (dart pub add jinja, vendor script, copy basecoat.dart), Jinja layout and page templates that work on Dart's jinja package, a server that renders through the Basecoat environment, and embedded templates for the compiled binary.
assertions: Adds the jinja package and vendors templates into templates/basecoat (vendor script or cp from node_modules/basecoat-css/templates/jinja)
Uses the bundled basecoat.dart Basecoat class to build the environment rather than a bare Environment
Templates are embedded for the binary (vendor script --embed with Basecoat.embedded, or an equivalent MapLoader)
Does not edit the vendored basecoat templates
Layout renders the sidebar and toaster through the macros
Current page is marked via the item's current flag / aria-current
Page template escapes project names with | e (no reliance on autoescaping)
Any {% call %} block imports its macro in that template; expression calls work as globals
Per-row select ids are derived from project.id
Templates avoid Python-only constructs unsupported on Dart jinja (string methods, negative indexes, positional args for defaulted params in own macros)
Loads Basecoat JavaScript in the layout
Lists the shell commands to run
